messages:
tara: FYI hit a weird combo on Windows + systemd-like service (we use NSSM) where credential rotation didn't take effect until service restart. thought worth discussing SDK defaults.
vik: Windows specifics? curious.
tara: rotate helper writes creds to %USERPROFILE%\.redwood\creds.json and sets REDWOOD_API_KEY in the user env; service runs under a machine account, so env change not visible until restart. SDK didn't detect file change either because our file watcher was inotify-only.
noelle: ahhh. inotify-only sucks on non-linux. we need cross-platform watch modes. propose REDWOOD_CRED_WATCH_MODE with values: poll|inotify|none. default = auto (inotify if available else poll).
av: ashok: +1 on explicit mode. Also add REDWOOD_CRED_POLL_INTERVAL (secs) to tune in heavy infra. default poll 5s for file, 2s for env.
vik: for services we should document that env-based rotations for system services require service restart, or apps must call Client.refreshCredentials() after you update creds file. we can't magically propagate user env to a machine service.
tara: agreed. we should update onboarding docs with OS-specific rotation recipes: systemd (systemctl restart svc or SIGHUP + refresh endpoint), Windows (NSSM or service restart), containers (export + exec into container + refresh), K8s (update secret + rollout or use sidecar to inject refresh).
noelle: also ran into HSM-backed provider nuance. HSM plugin returns short-lived assertion; the SDK was polling file mtime which never changed for HSM path. need to support provider hooks: provider can emit a small sentinel file or call client.refreshCredentials().
ashok: good point. add an optional hook spec: if REDWOOD_CRED_HOOK_SOCKET is set, SDK will listen on that Unix socket (or named pipe on Windows) for "refresh" messages. a simple local hook can push immediate refresh without polling.
tara: love that. but we should default to safe behavior: check env each request (cheap string compare) with 1s TTL cache, file check: mtime + 8-byte sha1 prefix, and fallback to hook if configured.
vik: parity note: python has a refresh hook API, js/go do not. we should standardize names: Client.refreshCredentials() and Client.on('credential-switched', cb) event. also export metric cred_source_switch_count for observability.
noelle: telemetry + logs are critical. log: "info: credential source switched from file->env" and metric increment. also emit a rare warning if REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID changes at runtime and refuse to apply it. project/org change must be process-restart.
ashok: implementation detail for file detection: do quick stat, if mtime differs then schedule hash compute; for tiny creds files it's cheap so prefer sync compute on first change then async later. on Windows use GetFileInformationByHandle to get change index.
tara: sample scripts: add examples/rotate-windows.ps1, examples/rotate-systemd.sh, and examples/rotate-hook.sh showing named-pipe notification. docs should show minimal pattern: write creds file, update env if applicable, signal app via refresh endpoint or socket.
vik: safety knobs: REDWOOD_CRED_HOTRELOAD=false to completely opt-out of hot-reload; REDWOOD_CRED_WATCH_MODE=none will disable watchers. default installations (hosted infra) probably set hot reload off for deterministic tests.
noelle: also add guidance for secret managers: when using KMS/HSM prefer short TTL tokens + proactive refresh in client with jitter; but avoid polling every request. for HSM, prefer push-hook model.
ops-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-specs/pull/47 - proposal: credential watch modes, refresh hook socket, refresh API, init-only project/org policy (tests added) :white_check_mark:
tara: thanks! I'll update the sample-app in examples/ with a Windows PS script and a systemd example and reference the new env vars in the SDK README. tagging @eng-sdk for implementation. :pray:
